steps.tx: The image shows a knee wound labeled upper third defect covered by a swung **medial gastrocnemius** muscle with its **sural pedicle** shown feeding the flap. This is the workhorse for **upper third tibial** wounds around the knee because nearby calf muscle reaches easily and brings strong blood supply. Remember it when the defect sits high and local muscle remains available for rotation.
steps.say: This view shows the inner calf muscle swung forward to cover an open knee wound. The label marks the upper third defect over the joint, with the sural vessels feeding the muscle belly from behind. This matters because high wounds near the knee have a ready local muscle option with rich blood flow, so they do not need a distant free flap. Think calf muscle for knee and high shin cover.

vis.alt: Medial view of the knee showing the medial gastrocnemius muscle rotated forward to cover an upper third defect with the sural pedicle visible.
vis.caption: Gastrocnemius muscle covering a high knee wound, Illustration: StewardMD original.

Microvascular free flap coverage with distant tissue

steps.say: Three workhorse free flaps are supplying lower extremity reconstruction. Anterolateral thigh flap with gracilis muscle is pairing bulk with delicacy. Latissimus dorsi flap is covering the vastest wounds. Long reliable pedicles are feeding distant transfers. Thigh with groin and back are supplying spare parts.
steps.tx: Three workhorse **free flaps** are supplying lower extremity reconstruction. **Anterolateral thigh (ALT) flap** with **gracilis muscle** is pairing bulk with delicacy. **Latissimus dorsi flap** is covering the vastest wounds. Long reliable pedicles are feeding distant transfers from thigh, groin, and back donor sites.

steps.tx: **Godina principle** is ordering **definitive flap coverage within 72 hours** of **open tibia fractures**. Early definitive flaps are slashing **osteomyelitis** with **nonunion** and **flap failure** together. Three-day cover is preventing bone infection, nonunion, and late loss.
